This means that features such as echoing input characters, line buffering, and\n//! special character processing (e.g., CTRL-C for SIGINT) are disabled. This is useful for\n//! applications that want to have complete control over the terminal input and output, processing\n//! each keystroke themselves.\n//!\n//! For example, in raw mode, the terminal will not perform line buffering on the input, so the\n//! application will receive each key press as it is typed, instead of waiting for the user to\n//! press enter. This makes it suitable for real-time applications like text editors,\n//! terminal-based games, and more.\n//!\n//! The alternate screen is a separate buffer that some terminals provide, distinct from the main\n//! screen. When activated, the terminal will display the alternate screen, hiding the current\n//! content of the main screen. Applications can write to this screen as if it were the regular\n//! terminal display, but when the application exits, the terminal will switch back to the main\n//! screen, and the contents of the alternate screen will be cleared. This is useful for\n//! applications like text editors or terminal games that want to use the full terminal window\n//! without disrupting the command line or other terminal content.\n//!\n//! This enables the\n//! application to handle and respond to mouse actions, providing a more interactive and graphical\n//! user experience within the terminal. It's particularly useful for applications like\n//! terminal-based games, text editors, or other programs that require more direct interaction from\n//! the user.\n//!\n//! It provides methods for drawing content, manipulating\n/// the cursor, and clearing the terminal screen.\n///\n/// Most applications should not call the methods on `CrosstermBackend` directly, but will instead\n/// use the [`Terminal`] struct, which provides a more ergonomic interface.\n///\n/// Usually applications will enable raw mode and switch to alternate screen mode after creating\n/// a `CrosstermBackend`. This is done by calling [`crossterm::terminal::enable_raw_mode`] and\n/// [`crossterm::terminal::EnterAlternateScreen`] (and the corresponding disable/leave functions\n/// when the application exits). This is not done automatically by the backend because it is\n/// possible that the application may want to use the terminal for other purposes (like showing\n/// help text) before entering alternate screen mode.\n///\n/// # Example\n///\n/// ```rust,no_run\n/// use std::io::{stderr, stdout};\n///\n/// use ratatui::{\n///     crossterm::{\n///         terminal::{\n///             disable_raw_mode, enable_raw_mode, EnterAlternateScreen, LeaveAlternateScreen,\n///         },\n///         ExecutableCommand,\n///     },\n///     prelude::*,\n/// };\n///\n/// let mut backend = CrosstermBackend::new(stdout());\n/// // or\n/// let backend = CrosstermBackend::new(stderr());\n/// let mut terminal = Terminal::new(backend)?;\n///\n/// enable_raw_mode()?;\n/// stdout().execute(EnterAlternateScreen)?;\n///\n/// terminal.clear()?;\n/// terminal.draw(|frame| {\n///     // -- snip --\n/// })?;\n///\n/// stdout().execute(LeaveAlternateScreen)?;\n/// disable_raw_mode()?;\n///\n/// # std::io::Result::Ok(())\n/// ```\n///\n/// See the the [Examples] directory for more examples. content {\n            // Move the cursor if the previous location was not (x - 1, y)\n            if !matches!(last_pos, Some(p) if x == p.x + 1 && y == p.y) {\n                queue!(self.writer,               let index = self.buffer.index_of(self.pos.0, self.pos.1);\n259\t                &mut self.buffer.content[..index]\n260\t            }\n261\t            ClearType::CurrentLine => {\n262\t                let line_start_index = self.buffer.index_of(0, self.pos.1);\n263\t                let line_end_index = self.buffer.index_of(self.buffer.area.width - 1, self.pos.1);\n264\t                &mut self.buffer.content[line_start_index..=line_end_index]\n265\t            }\n266\t            ClearType::UntilNewLine => {\n267\t                let index = self.buffer.index_of(self.pos.0, self.pos.1);\n268\t                let line_end_index = self.buffer.index_of(self.buffer.area.width - 1, self.pos.1);\n269\t                &mut self.buffer.content[index..=line_end_index]\n270\t            }\n271\t        };\n272\t        for cell in region {\n273\t            cell.reset();\n274\t        }\n275\t        Ok(())\n276\t    }\n277\t\n278\t    /// Inserts n line breaks at the current cursor position.\n279\t    ///\n280\t    /// After the insertion, the cursor x position will be incremented by 1 (unless it's already\n281\t    /// at the end of line). This is a common behaviour of terminals in raw mode.\n282\t    ///\n283\t    /// If the number of lines to append is fewer than the number of lines in the buffer after the\n284\t    /// cursor y position then the cursor is moved down by n rows.\n285\t    ///\n286\t    /// If the number of lines to append is greater than the number of lines in the buffer after\n287\t    /// the cursor y position then that number of empty lines (at most the buffer's height in this\n288\t    /// case but this limit is instead replaced with scrolling in most backend implementations) will\n289\t    /// be added after the current position and the cursor will be moved to the last row.\n290\t    fn append_lines(&mut self, line_count: u16) -> io::Result<()> {\n291\t        let Position { x: cur_x, y: cur_y } = self.get_cursor_position()?;\n292\t        let Rect { width, height, .. } = self.buffer.area;\n293\t\n294\t        // the next column ensuring that we don't go past the last column\n295\t        let new_cursor_x = cur_x.saturating_add(1).min(width.saturating_sub(1));\n296\t\n297\t        let max_y = height.saturating_sub(1);\n298\t        let lines_after_cursor = max_y.saturating_sub(cur_y);\n299\t\n300\t        if line_count > lines_after_cursor {\n301\t            // We need to insert blank lines at the bottom and scroll the lines from the top into\n302\t            // scrollback.\n303\t            let scroll_by: usize = (line_count - lines_after_cursor).into();\n304\t            let width: usize = self.buffer.area.width.into();\n305\t            let cells_to_scrollback = self.buffer.content.len().min(width * scroll_by);\n306\t\n307\t            append_to_scrollback(\n308\t                &mut self.scrollback,\n309\t                self.buffer.content.splice(\n310\t                    0..cells_to_scrollback,\n311\t                    iter::repeat_with(Default::default).take(cells_to_scrollback),\n312\t                ),\n313\t            );\n314\t            self.buffer.content.rotate_left(cells_to_scrollback);\n315\t            append_to_scrollback(\n316\t                &mut self.scrollback,\n317\t                iter::repeat_with(Default::default).take(width * scroll_by - cells_to_scrollback),\n318\t            );\n319\t        }\n320\t\n321\t        let new_cursor_y = cur_y.saturating_add(line_count).min(max_y);\n322\t        self.set_cursor_position(Position::new(new_cursor_x, new_cursor_y))?;\n323\t\n324\t        Ok(())\n325\t    }\n326\t\n327\t    fn size(&self) -> io::Result<Size> {\n328\t        Ok(self.buffer.area.as_size())\n329\t    }\n330\t\n331\t    fn window_size(&mut self) -> io::Result<WindowSize> {\n332\t        // Some arbitrary window pixel size, probably doesn't need much testing.\n333\t        const WINDOW_PIXEL_SIZE: Size = Size {\n334\t            width: 640,\n335\t            height: 480,\n336\t        };\n337\t        Ok(WindowSize {\n338\t            columns_rows: self.buffer.area.as_size(),\n339\t            pixels: WINDOW_PIXEL_SIZE,\n340\t        })\n341\t    }\n342\t\n343\t    fn flush(&mut self) -> io::Result<()> {\n344\t        Ok(())\n345\t    }\n346\t}\n347\t\n348\t/// Append the provided cells to the bottom of a scrollback buffer. The number of cells must be a\n349\t/// multiple of the buffer's width. If the scrollback buffer ends up larger than 65535 lines tall,\n350\t/// then lines will be removed from the top to get it down to size.\n351\tfn append_to_scrollback(scrollback: &mut Buffer, cells: impl IntoIterator<Item = Cell>) {\n352\t    scrollback.content.extend(cells);\n353\t    let width = scrollback.area.width as usize;\n354\t    let new_height = (scrollback.content.len() / width).min(u16::MAX as usize);\n355\t    let keep_from = scrollback\n356\t        .content\n357\t        .len()\n358\t        .saturating_sub(width * u16::MAX as usize);\n359\t    scrollback.content.drain(0..keep_from);\n360\t    scrollback.area.height = new_height as u16;\n361\t}\n362\t\n363\t#[cfg(test)]\n364\tmod tests {\n365\t    use itertools::Itertools as _;\n366\t\n367\t
